long_biography.plain_text:
A farm upbringing in McMinn County, Tennessee, preceded Franklin Haney's career in law and property. He paid his way through the University of Tennessee by selling books, then earned a law degree at George Washington University. After working in public service and private practice, he founded FLH Company in 1967. Early developments included apartments, hotels, parking garages and government offices in Tennessee before the business expanded across the South and into Washington.

FLH used structured financing and long government leases to develop major office and infrastructure projects. It also bought beverage distributors in the 1980s, but property remained its core business. The company describes a cumulative development portfolio exceeding $10 billion. That figure measures projects undertaken by the family business, not Franklin Haney's personal net worth or liquid holdings. Haney remains listed as chairman and founder, while his son Frank Haney Jr. is president and operates the company. That transition establishes successor management, not a disclosed inheritance or estate transfer. No credible death record matches the developer; current corporate and identity records support the existing Alive status.
